```
cd /srv/qellys && sudo -u qellys python3 -c "
import glob, json, os, time
from engine import oddsbudget as ob
for r in ob.decisions(since=time.time() - 30 * 3600, lane='cbb')[-25:]: print(r['iso'], 'bought' if r['ok'] else 'held', r.get('credits'), r['reason'][:170])
for f in sorted(glob.glob('data/cache/odds_event_cbb_*.json'), key=os.path.getmtime)[-8:]:
    d = json.load(open(f)); n = {}
    for b in d.get('bookmakers') or []:
        for m in b.get('markets') or []:
            if str(m.get('key') or '').startswith('player_'):
                c = n.setdefault(m['key'], [0, 0, set()]); c[2].add(b.get('key'))
                for o in m.get('outcomes') or []: c[0 if str(o.get('name')).lower() == 'over' else 1] += 1
    print(time.strftime('%m-%d %H:%M', time.localtime(os.path.getmtime(f))), d.get('away_team'), '@', d.get('home_team'), {k: (v[0], v[1], len(v[2])) for k, v in sorted(n.items())})
"
```

**AAB. Every parlay says Safe, Balanced or Pop and names its one book; NBA and NHL picks show a Green, Yellow or Red
price** (step 816; 20 November). Nothing to run. You said yes to both. (1) The class, on every two-leg and three-leg
parlay, by the bars in your v3.1 instructions: Safe is every leg 64% or better and 40% together; Balanced is every
leg 60% or better and 36% together; Pop is 25% together; under 25% the card says Long shot. Each card says why it is
not the class above. In the NBA and hockey, Safe also needs every leg at a Green price and Balanced one, as your
section 10 says. Football's classes use the chances alone: its numbers are tied to their prices now, so no football
leg can sit over its price. A three-leg parlay comes out Pop nearly every time, which is what three legs are by your
own targets (25-30%). Touchdown pairs are not classed. The dollar stakes in your instructions are yours and stay off
the site. (2) The one book: each parlay names the one sportsbook that has every leg at its number (the one paying
most on them), or says no one book in our pull does. A same-game parlay is placed at one book, and each leg shows
the best price across the books, so this says where the whole ticket can go. It is a line on the card, not yet a
rule; the heartbeat's `one_book` counts how many tickets have one, and that count decides whether to require it
(decision below). (3) The price grade, on NBA and NHL player picks: Green where the price needs no more than our
number, Yellow up to 2 points more, Red beyond that. It is on the game report's pick card, Report Picks and the Most
Likely card. Every pick stays posted. Your instructions say never to post a Red; I did not adopt that, because Red-
priced picks have hit as often as Green ones. What the grade sorts is the money. Public receipts to 20 November,
props at -250 or better, each pick once, at a chance of 60% or better: NBA Green 673 picks hit 62.6% and made 2.6% a
bet, Yellow 399 hit 66.9% and made 0.3%, Red 804 hit 67.5% and lost 1.6%; NHL Green 1,010 hit 66.5% and made 1.9%,
Yellow 542 hit 68.8% and made 1.9%, Red 744 hit 66.9% and lost 2.6%. Under 60% the grade sorted nothing: every grade
made money, and the NBA's Red-priced picks at 50-60% hit 66.9% where we said 57.3% (614), so there our number is the
one running low (the open decision on letting the record raise an NBA or NHL chance). Each card says how picks at
its chance and grade have done on our own record once 20 have settled, which is the line to read beside the colour.
Football gets no grade: there the Green ones were the picks we had overrated (NFL 2,232 hit 54.6% where we said
71.7%; college 1,133 hit 53.4% where we said 72.7%). Also: the Record page splits each league's two-leg and three-
leg parlays by class, read from the chances and prices each was journaled with, so earlier tickets count; and Ask
Qellys can say a ticket's class, its one book and a pick's price grade. Where to look: any report's Parlays section
and pick card; the heartbeat's `ticket_classes`, `one_book` and `price_grade` for each league. `QB_PRICE_GRADE=off`
in the service's environment turns the grade off. Decision for you: should a parlay have to be one that a single
book prices whole? I would look at the weekend's `one_book` counts first.

leg 14 of 20 beside three-leg 22 of 43. The Record page lists two-leg parlays for every league again, and football's

**ZZ. Your v3.1 instructions, beside the board's own logic** (step 814; 20 November). Nothing to run. You pasted
"NFL Prop Bot — Master Instructions v3.1" and said to use it alongside what the site does, replacing nothing. I
mapped all of it in `docs/NFL_BET_CHECKING_METHOD.md`, section by section. Most of it the site already did: the −250
cap, tickets that win together, the four scripts and what each leg needs, the take-at price, no more than two
tickets on a leg, and your learning rule (a market 8 points under its rate over 20 legs drops a tier) is the board's
record check as written. What was new and is now in, football only, every pick still on the board: (1) the touchdown
rule's fallback is 40% with the red-zone role at a plus price paying 6% over our number; it had passed the role at
any price, and the NFL's 63 touchdown picks at 40-45% hit 36.5%. (2) Kept off parlays: a backup back's yardage (a
back behind the lead carrier with under 8 carries a game, your own line between roles; my first cut called every
non-lead back a backup and cost college four tickets on its first board, so I narrowed it the same evening), a
quarterback's rush-attempt under, and a quarterback's rushing over where the charting has at least half the carries
as scrambles, so Jayden Daniels' rushing yards on your own 12 November ticket still count as a leg. (3) Behind a new
starting quarterback with under 50 passes, a catch or receiving-yards pick tops out at Worth a look and is no parlay
leg. (4) Two pass catchers from one team share no touchdown pair; a back beside a catcher still does. (5) The big-
favorite rule caps pass attempts only; it had capped a favorite's completions and yards, which v3.1 says not to
fade. The heartbeat's `pick_fates` now counts `our_rule` (picks kept off parlays by these). What I did not adopt,
and why: the Green / Yellow / Red price grade. It posts a leg only when our number beats the price, and on the
record our number has not earned that in football: the 677 NFL board picks shown above their price said 68.5% and
hit 56.1%, the 617 college props 66.9% and 55.1%, while the picks at or under their price hit what we said. So the
site keeps the stricter version (show the price's number, post the take-at price). The 45% touchdown clause keeps no
price test for the same reason: the 127 NFL picks at 45% and under their price hit 57.5%, the 6 above theirs hit 2.
Five decisions are listed in that doc and in my message.

**ZY. A college price with one side quoted is not a second opinion** (step 813; 20 November). Nothing to run. The
same record showed a second leak ZX does not reach, in picks at or under their price. The college props whose best
price was DraftKings' (136, every one an over) hit 54.4% where we said 64.3% and the price said 67.6%, short in both
halves of the season (57%, then 52%). The 119 of them at -180 or steeper hit 53.8%; FanDuel's 220 at those prices
hit 65.0%, and we had said 64.9% of both. A book that quotes only the over keeps its whole cut on that side, and the
board's market check was reading such a price with an assumed cut taken off, then counting it as the market agreeing
with us. Now a college prop whose number no book quotes both sides of gets no credit from the market check (its card
says "no book quotes both sides of this number"); it stays on the board on our own number, the matchup and the
record. One thing I could not measure: the public file does not keep whether a quote had one side, so that
DraftKings' picks are the over-only ones is my inference from their all being overs. The heartbeat's college
`price_ceiling` now counts them (`one_sided`), so Saturday's board will say; if it reads 0 the rule is touching
nothing and I will look again at those picks on the box's own journal. It goes off with ZX's switch.

**ZX. A college football prop is never shown above its own price** (step 812; 20 November). Nothing to run. You
asked for the NFL's pick work on every other league, college football and the NBA first. I measured before changing
anything, on the site's own public file of every graded pick (57,100 rows). The NBA's and hockey's boards hit at or
above what they claim (NBA 64.5% where we said 61.1% over 3,086 picks; their report picks 70% and 73%), so their
numbers stay. College football's did not: of 1,525 graded board props since 26 September, the 617 we showed above
their own best price said 66.9% and hit 55.1%, where the price itself said 57.1%; the 908 at or under their price
said 57.7% and hit 58.5%. The NFL's fix reads three books' fair price, which college props almost never have (8 of
2,087 picks on 31 October), so college could not use it. Every prop has its own price, though, so a college prop is
now shown at the chance a bet at its best price needs to break even whenever ours runs above it, and the card says
so ("we said 70%; a bet at its best price needs 58% to break even..."). Tried on the same record, that number was
closer to what happened in eight of the nine weeks, and each day's five likeliest props hit 66.9% against 61.1% when
ranked by our own number (175 picks). The report card, the tiers and the parlay legs read the board, so they follow.
A pick shown at its price's number is never a Top pick on the price agreeing with it. Picks already on paper are
left alone, so the paper record keeps measuring our own claim. Props only: too few game lines (16) and touchdowns
(9) sat above their price to judge. The heartbeat's college line now carries `price_ceiling` (props read, priced,
above, moved, already posted) and `board_tiers`, counts only. To switch it off: `cd /srv/qellys && sudo
./deploy/setenv.sh QB_PRICE_CEILING off && sudo systemctl restart qellys`.

**ZW. Basketball's tickets say their size; a read's chance is grey** (step 811; 20 November). Nothing to run. Drawn
and looked at, a basketball game on Report Picks: its six tickets read "Parlay 1" to "Parlay 3" and then "Two-leg
parlay 1" to "Two-leg parlay 3" under a heading that said "Parlays and pairs", with no pairs. A game that posts both
sizes now names both ("Three-leg parlay 1"), the heading says "Parlays" where there are no scorer pairs, and a
read's chance is drawn grey, as a dropped pick's is, not the green of a pick we stake. Last night's tickets with an
under leg against those without: the NBA's three-leg 3 of 7 and 0 of 2, two-leg 2 of 4 and 1 of 1; the NHL's
three-leg 11 of 19 and 6 of 6, two-leg 9 of 14 and 4 of 4. One night, too few to say anything about two unders
sharing a ticket.

**ZV. A matchup read's own pick carries the flag** (step 810; 20 November). Nothing to run. After ZU the heartbeat's
pick census still counted 10 NFL report picks as `refused_unreliable` against 2 said as reads. A matchup read's own
Most Likely pick is a short copy of the board's row (`likely._pick_brief`), and the copy left out the flag that says
our number can't price the market. So those picks still said "take it at" on the reads and went on the record as
bets. The copy keeps the flag now: they say "A read, not a bet", stay off the record, and any still open are taken
off the next time their board is journaled.

**ZU. A read on the card, said once** (step 809; 20 November). Nothing to run. Drawn and looked at: on the picks
card a read wore the board's tier ("Top pick") beside its "Read, not a bet" tag, and the line under the tag began
with the same words. A read now wears only its tag, the line says why once ("A market we can rank but not price yet,
so it isn't counted on the record"), and the card's note says every bet comes before a read. The heartbeat's pick
census counts a read as `read`, ahead of any other fate, since no ticket takes one. A report's header no longer
prints a reading time it does not have. On the record (each game's starting set, read off the public record file):
the NBA's two-leg tickets 12 of 16 (+12.3 units) and its three-leg tickets 6 of 27 (−6.0 units). Those three-leg
tickets' legs hit 58 of 81 (72%) against the 66% we said, 19 of their 21 losses were one leg away, and 6 of 27 is
within the noise of the 30% we stated, so their build is unchanged. Hockey's three-leg tickets are 22 of 43 (+18.1
units) and its goal-scorer pairs 6 of 41 (+11.5 units).

**ZT. Basketball's two-leg parlays, and reads that are not bets** (step 808; 20 November). Nothing to run. Ethan, to
the two questions in the ZS report: "yes to both, do 2-leg nba parlays and label the yardage picks". Basketball's
books post no anytime scorer, so the NBA, college basketball and the WNBA now post three two-leg player-prop parlays
a game where football posts its scorer pairs. They are built from the report's own picks like the three-leg ones,
two legs at 63% or better (40% together), filled the same way when a game is short, journaled and graded as two-leg
parlays, and counted on the heartbeat (`sgp_twos`, `twos_short`). Football and hockey still post none, and the
record leaves any old ones of theirs off. A report pick on a market our model can rank but not price (the NFL's
rushing and receiving yards: 19 of its 47 report picks on 20 November) now says "A read, not a bet" on the report's
card and reads, with no price to take it at, and on Report Picks, which leaves it out of its counts; a finished
game's card leaves it out of "Our picks", and Ask says so too. The report book never journals one: those journaled
before the label and still open are taken off the next time their board is journaled, and graded ones keep their
grade. Matchup picks never carried the flag the Most Likely rows do, so a yardage matchup pick read as a bet; they
carry it now. On the picks card, which ranks four picks a game (six on a featured one), every bet now comes before
any read, so a read never takes a bet's place on the card or the record.

**ZS. Follow-ups to ZR** (step 807; 20 November). Nothing to run. The report's one-line summary names the touchdown
pair our research ranks best (a pair with a stand-in scorer comes last), not just the likeliest one. The heartbeat's
reasons a game is short now count every trio the fill could try: since ZR the last level tries them all, and two NFL
games read "conflicts" only because the old count looked at the report's own picks. The reasons are now `conflicts`
(no three of its legs fit), `under_floor` (none reaches 15%) and `legs_used` (trios clear, but each usable leg
already rides on two tickets); live at 10:15 ET the three short NFL games all read `legs_used`. The NFL's 19 of 47
report picks counted `refused_book` (no real book) were nothing of the kind: a new count, `pick_book_why`, showed
all 19 were Most Likely rows a real book prices on markets our calibration does not trust ("not bettable": the fit
ran off its range, mostly yardage). They now count as `refused_unreliable`, and `refused_book` means what it says.
Those picks still show on the NFL reports as picks with our chance, while the Most Likely page labels the same rows
"a read on who hits rather than a card"; that is a question for you in the report. The members' pitch on Report
Picks and the More page said the parlays are built "only from" the report's picks; they now say three and three a
game, the report's picks first, any other leg named on its ticket.

**ZR. Every game posts three three-leg parlays and three scorer pairs** (step 806; 20 November). Nothing to run.
Ethan: "We should be making the 3 best parlays possible with the data we have including the game report with the
best possible props we have", and, asked what that meant a game: "i want 3 3 leg player prop parlays and 3 2 leg td
prop parlays". Each game now posts exactly that. The three-leg parlays take the report's own picks first. When those
can't make three, the game fills in this order: two of the report's picks with one other prop at 55% or better; then
the game's Most Likely picks in the picks' places, on a ticket at 25% or better; and last the game's best props, any
of them, on a ticket down to 15%. Each step only adds to what the one before it made, every leg that isn't one of
the report's picks is named on its ticket, and a set of tickets that can all win together still comes ahead of one
that can't. The scorer pairs (touchdown pairs in football, goal-scorer pairs in hockey) work the same way: a game
short of three takes its next scorers, a weaker research case first (priced high enough but under 4 of the 13
research points), then a longer price (down to 20% in the NFL, 22% in college, 18% in hockey), never an avoid read
or a scorer with no red-zone role, each stand-in named on its pair. Basketball has no scorer market, so its games
post the three three-leg parlays only. The two-leg player-prop parlays are retired, and with them the hold that kept
them on paper (engine/parlayhold is deleted; the night no longer runs it). Their tickets stay in the journal and
stay off the Record page. New measure: each filled ticket is journaled with how it was made up (a `fill` column:
one, board, props or stand_in), and from today each league's parlay card on the Record page says how each way has
done once two ways have tickets, e.g. "By how they were made up, since 20 Nov: the report's own picks 5 of 12 hit ·
the game's best props 1 of 4 hit". That is how we'll know whether the filled tickets earn their place. The heartbeat
drops `sgp_twos` and adds `td_short` (games still short of three pairs), `td_filled` (pairs a stand-in filled) and
`threes_props_filled` (tickets the game's best props made up). Watch it on Sunday: `sgp_threes` should be close to 3
a game, `td_pairs` close to 3 a football game, and `threes_short` and `td_short` small.

**ZQ. A game's posted parlays stay posted until a leg breaks** (step 805; 20 November). Nothing to run. This is the
real fix for "30 parlays a game". Every board build used to pick each game's parlays from scratch, so a line moving
half a point could reorder them and the board posted a new set; one NFL game went through 19 versions of its three-
leg parlays between Thursday and Sunday. Now the parlays a game posted last build are tried first and posted again
for as long as each one still qualifies: every leg is still available (still in the report, a real book still prices
it, nobody on it has been ruled out), and the parlay still clears its chance floor and fits with the others. A
parlay is matched on player, market and side, so when a book moves a line the same parlay stays up with the new line
and price. Only a parlay that breaks gets replaced, and only its own spot changes. This covers the three-leg and
two-leg parlays and the scorer pairs (touchdown pairs in football, goal-scorer pairs in hockey) in every league. A
one-team parlay stays only while it is still the likelier read, and a stand-in parlay (built from Most Likely picks
or other props when the report was short) gives way once the report's own picks can make a real one. The heartbeat
now shows, per league, how many of the last build's parlays were posted again and how many were replaced ("posted":
kept and replaced, counts only). Watch it on Sunday morning: replaced should be a small number next to kept.

**ZP. A finished game lists one set of parlays, never a stack of versions** (step 804; 20 November). Nothing to run.
Ethan sent two screenshots of Report Picks' "How our reports did" with rows like "Parlays 0 of 28" and "1 of 42":
"why do we have 30 parlays being made per game?? There should only be 3 parlays made per game". Those were games
from before 16 November, when the site began keeping the set each report carried at kickoff. With no kept set, the
list showed every version the board posted that week as lines moved (the NFL rebuilds a game's parlays dozens of
times between Thursday and Sunday). None of those were ever counted on the Record, but listing them made it look
like 30 parlays a game. Now a finished game lists only the set its report carried at kickoff. A game with no kept
set lists no parlays and says why, under its picks. The "the board also posted 19 earlier versions" line is gone
from kept games too, and so is the Record's "The 1,234 others the board posted and replaced" count. The game's own
page reads the same kept set from the record, and so does Ask. Each game still posts up to 3 three-leg parlays, up
to 2 two-leg parlays and, in football, 3 touchdown pairs. The next step (ZQ) makes a game's posted parlays stay put
until a leg actually breaks, so the board stops replacing them every time a line moves.

**ZO. The pick count says which picks are waiting on their game's props** (step 803; 20 November). Nothing to run.
After ZL went live, the NFL board rebuilt and still said 19 of its 47 report picks had "no real book", this time
correctly: no list held them at a real price. Some of those are simply Monday night's game, whose props aren't
bought yet, and that says nothing about the picks. So a pick in a game with fewer than 10 priced props (the same
rule the builder already uses to decide a game's props are bought) now counts as "props not bought", and only the
rest stay "no real book". Those remaining ones are a player and market no book prices, and that's what's worth
chasing next. Counts only, like the rest of the heartbeat.

**ZN. Three small fixes found while building ZM** (step 802; 20 November). Nothing to run. (1) On a live game's
page, the ⋯ menu (Hide the score, the TV delay) could snap shut by itself if the live update redrew the page right
as you tapped it. The test suite caught it on a busy machine. The page now keeps whatever is open before it redraws.
(2) A parlay leg on Report Picks could read "over 1.5 fg3m" for a moment, until the record's word list arrived. A
leg now uses its own word ("3-pointers made"). (3) Ask Qellys lists every report parlay likeliest first, but it
wasn't told which tickets our own card says to pass on, or which games have already started, so it could name one of
those as tonight's best. Each ticket now says so, the same way the new strip leaves them out. Also in plain words
now: the Line Shopping page (no more "z=11.6", "arbs" or "juice"), and seven new glossary entries: parlay, leg,
push, sharp book, steam, arbitrage and middle.

**ZM. Report Picks leads with the likeliest tickets today** (step 801; 20 November). Nothing to run. One of my own
ideas, for your "make better selections". A night posts every game's two- and three-leg parlays, one fold per game,
and nothing said which ones to look at first. The record answers that: the likeliest tickets hit most. The two-leg
tickets have hit 26 of 36 in hockey and basketball since the 16th (hockey 14 of 20, basketball 12 of 16), against 28
of 70 for the three-leg ones. So the Today tab now opens, under the day's line, on the three likeliest tickets of
the games still to play, at most one per game. Each line gives the game, how many legs, the legs in words, our
chance, and the price to take it at. Tapping a line opens that game, where the full ticket is. Scorer pairs, games
already started, and any ticket our own card says to pass on (no book likely pays enough for it) are left out, and a
day with fewer than two games to choose from shows nothing. It is members only, like the rest of the tab.

**ZL. The pick count says why a pick missed the parlays** (step 800; 20 November). Nothing to run. The heartbeat
counts what became of each game report pick: on a ticket, a stand-in, under the bar, or turned down and why. On this
morning's NFL board it said 16 of 42 picks were turned down for "no real book". That number was wrong. A pick sits
in several lists (Most Likely, the pool, the priced props), and the count said "no book" whenever one of those lists
held it without a price, even when another list had a real price and the pick was turned down for its price or its
number. Now a list with a real price decides the reason, "no book" means no list has one, and a player ruled out is
still said first. Nothing on the site or in any ticket changes; the count is how I find which picks the parlays lose
and why, and the next NFL build will say the real reasons for those 16.

**ZK. The game reports stay a member's, all of it** (step 799; 20 November). Nothing to run. Your call this morning:
you first said free accounts should get the report without its picks and parlays, then took it back: the game
reports are not free. That is how the site already worked, and I checked every door on the live site. The public
board files carry no report (the NBA's says 9 reports are locked, the NFL's 13, and not one of a report's words is
in either); a free account's game page has the report taken out with one lock card in its place; Ask refuses a free
account before it reads anything; a finished game's report needs the membership; Report Picks is a member's page;
the new live tickets are a count behind a lock; and the sign-up table and the plans page list the reports under
members. One gap closed: the drive simulation the report quotes ("our simulation of the game, drive by drive, 4,000
times: the Lions 58%") rode every public NFL game row, readable by anyone who opened the file, though the page never
showed it to a free account. It is now cut from the public copy and stays on the members' copy. The check the site
runs at every start, and before it serves a public board, now looks inside each row as well as at each key, so a
field newly named paid is cut at the next restart instead of waiting for its board's next build (the public NFL file
up this morning, built at 05:52, still had it). The game's facts stay free (the line, the venue, the weather, the
injuries, the scan's numbers), and so does the Record: after a game ends, its graded picks and parlays show there
with a check or an X, the way every book's results do, because the public record is the proof. Tell me if you want
those hidden from free accounts too. Your decision is written beside the paid keys in engine/gate.py and held door
by door by tests/test_the_game_report_is_a_members.py.

**ZJ. The game reports' parlays, followed live** (step 798; 19 November). Nothing to run. One of my own ideas, since
you asked for some: a member who played a report's ticket had nowhere to watch it. The Live tab followed the Edge
and Most Likely picks and the slips a reader saved; the tickets every game report builds went quiet at kickoff, and
those are the bets you care most about. Now, for every game under way in every league, the Live tab has "Our report
parlays, live" under the scoreboard: each posted ticket with a dot a leg and where it stands ("Alive: 1 of 3 legs
in", "One leg to go: Scottie Barnes", "Won: all 3 legs hit", "Lost: Jalen Brunson missed"), and under it each leg
with the player's face, the pick, the number so far against its line as a bar, and what it still needs in one line
("Needs 2 more", "Can give up 10 more"). An under past its number is lost at once and an over past its number is in,
whatever the clock says. The same tickets sit on each live game's own page, at the end of its picks rail, in every
sport. A game that has ended keeps its tickets there, settled on the final box, until the board moves on. It costs
nothing: the tickets are the board's own (a started game's are kept as they stood), and each leg's number comes off
the scoreboard and box files the live loop already writes every twelve seconds. The page asks every 30 seconds while
a followed game is being played, one answer serves every member for eight seconds, and the report's script is only
loaded when there is a ticket to draw. Paper tickets are not listed. It is a member's: a free account gets the
site's lock card saying how many tickets are being followed in how many games, and no ticket (the report's script is
never even loaded for them). A game you saved for later keeps its numbers to itself. Ask reads the same thing ("is
our Knicks parlay still alive?"). Checked by tests/test_a_reports_parlays_are_followed_live.py and
tests/test_pbp_our_picks.py.

**ZI. The game report's folded titles say their answers, and the wording pass** (step 797; 19 November). Nothing to
run. I went through the game report page as a member sees it, start to end, on a phone. Three things. First, the
report reads with our picks and the short version open and everything else folded to its title, and a title said
what a section was about, not what it found: "Who we think wins" kept its answer a tap away at the top of every
report. Where a section's finding fits in a few words its title now carries it at the right: "Who we think wins ·
Lions 60%", "The market · DET by 3 at home, total 52.5", "How the units rank · GB 3 edges, DET 3", "Injuries and
availability · 2 listed, 1 out", "Parlays for this game · 8 tickets", "Players to watch · 2 breakouts, 1 fade", "Weather and venue
· Indoors". Each is read off the section's own blocks, so it cannot disagree with the section, every league's report
gets them, and the page hides one once its fold is open (each thing once). A started game's report is the one kept
from before the game, so its titles gain theirs at its next game. Second, the replay panel on the game page spoke in
the code's words: "both 0% (+0.0pt vs independent legs)" and "the sim prices nothing until the public reconciliation
says it should". It now says "DET covers the spread 48% · the game goes over 50% · both happen 26%, 2.1 points more
often than two unrelated bets would" (the last part only when it is a real difference), and "A picture of the game,
not a pick: none of our prices come from it." A game plan row could show a feed's raw key ("rush_att"); it is said
in words. Third, the wording pass you asked for, on the lines a reader meets most: every "de-vigged" outside the
calculator that is named for it now says what it means ("the books' fair price (their cut taken out)"), a "Brier"
comparison in a sentence says "our chances have been closer to what happened than the books' fair prices (forecast
error 0.21 against 0.22; lower is better)", the league pages' sub-lines say what the page holds instead of how the
model is built, and two tooltips that cited the spec's section numbers say the thing itself. The metric's name stays
on the model scorecards, where the glossary defines it. Also here: the chance bar on a parlay card fills as the card
is drawn (never for a reader who asked for less motion), and Ask's record tool is told it holds how each kind of
report pick has done. Checked by tests/test_a_folded_section_says_its_answer.py, tests/test_drivesim.py,
tests/test_a_parlay_card_says_each_thing_once.py and tests/test_the_nfl_board_trusts_the_price.py.

**ZH. A parlay card you can read at a glance** (step 796; 19 November). Nothing to run. The graphics pass, started
where you look most. A ticket's chance was the first words of a row of small grey type ("49% by our numbers · fair
+104 · take it at +114 or better"); it now stands large beside a bar filled to it, green at 40% and up, gold from
25%, amber for a long shot, with the rest of the line under it. Each leg wears its player's face (the club's helmet
where the board has none), which stays beside the name when a long pick wraps, and a ticket's backups and caveats
are set as the small print they are: they were the largest type on the card. The same card draws on the game report
and on Report Picks. On Report Picks every pick said "Our picks" under its name, four times a game; the card's own
pick now says nothing, a matchup read's, a breakout candidate's or a fade's names itself, and a card pick a read
also backs says "Also a matchup read". The last-slate card reads the slate's day against your own calendar ("Today
so far" for games that ended this evening, "Last night", then the day). And one clock fix for readers outside the
East: a tip-off or first pitch is said whole in your zone, its day with its clock; it read "Thu, Nov 19 · 1:00 AM"
in London for a game at 8 PM Eastern. Football's kickoffs stay Eastern with "ET" on them, because the feed gives a
clock reading and no instant (your open question on that still stands). Checked by
tests/test_a_parlay_card_says_each_thing_once.py, tests/test_report_bets_have_their_own_book_and_page.py,
tests/test_the_last_slate_s_reports_are_summed_at_a_glance.py and tests/test_riding_stamps.py.

**ZG. The record says how each kind of report pick has done** (step 795; 19 November). Nothing to run. The first
night's count of what became of each report pick as a parlay leg (step ZD) read, for the NFL's games still to play:
39 picks, 18 of them legs a ticket can take, 8 a matchup read's own pick no ticket could take, 9 a row the board
holds and will not use, 2 in markets a parlay never carries, 1 benched and 1 priced at another number. Before a
matchup read's pick becomes a parlay leg I want to know it hits like the picks on the card, and nothing could say:
every report pick was journaled under one label. From this push each is journaled under the first place its report
shows it (Our picks, Matchup read, Breakout candidate, Fade), and a pick still open under the old label takes its
kind's, so Sunday's NFL picks count from the start. The Record page's game-report section shows the split once two
rows have results ("By where the report showed it"), the earlier picks as one row, and Ask Qellys reads the same.
The count of refused picks now says why: ruled out, no real book, past the -250 cap, or a number the Edge path
refuses. What this decides is whether matchup-read picks join the parlays; I will make that call on the split as
results come in, not before it. Checked by tests/test_report_bets_have_their_own_book_and_page.py,
tests/test_the_heartbeat_says_what_became_of_each_report_pick.py and
tests/test_ask_reads_the_reports_and_the_races.py.

**ZF. A game's page wears its two clubs, and the cards say each thing once** (step 794; 19 November). Nothing to
run. The colour work, continued: the page a game has before it starts and after it ends now sits on its two clubs'
colours, the away club from the left and the home club from the right, the way the live page, a team's page and a
player's page already wear theirs. It works with the colour setting off, sits over your own colours if you wear some
(the bar's tint stays yours: a game has two clubs and neither is you), fades in and out like every other colour
change, and hands the screen back when you leave. Two clubs in one colour, and the away side wears its second (Colts
at Lions is red against blue); a fight card has no clubs and keeps the site's look. Then I drew the paid cards the
way a member sees them and fixed what repeated or read wrong: Today's Top Pick from another league said its number
three times ("MEM -6.5 -6.5 -6.5 Spread"); the note under a carried Pick of the Day gave the server's clock, now
yours; a parlay card gave its price caution twice and listed one backup leg once for every leg (now once: "If any
leg is out or its number moves: ..."); a two-leg ticket said "Both legs here is"; the level strip could read "Level
NaN" for a moment; the Ask page's league row ran "NCAAB" into "WNBA" on phones; and the parlay builder's blurb reads
as one sentence. One guard in the engine: a report pick that carries its game's label is no longer mistaken for the
game bet when the parlays are built (it had not happened live; a test fixture found it). Checked by
tests/test_a_games_page_wears_its_two_clubs.py, tests/test_a_parlay_card_says_each_thing_once.py and
tests/test_potd_card.py.

**ZE. Last night's reports at a glance, and Ask Qellys knows the rebuilt parlays** (step 793; 19 November). Nothing
to run. One of mine, for the question you ask most days (did the picks hit, did the parlays): Report Picks now opens
with one card above today's picks that sums the newest day with a finished game. It reads, for example, "Last night,
12 games: Picks 54-20, +3.1 units · Three-leg parlays 9 of 20 · Two-leg parlays 8 of 12 · Goal-scorer pairs 1 of 4 ·
Who wins 7 of 12", with a way to each game's picks and tickets, check by check. The picks are counted at one unit a
pick at the price posted; the parlays are the set each report carried at the start, as the Record counts them; a
slate older than yesterday is said by its day ("Sunday, Nov 22"). It is free, as everything settled is, and every
league has it. The league's report record serves it (/api/report_record last_slate, engine/reportrecord.last_slate,
read again only when the archive or the journal moved); the card your phone last saw is drawn at once and corrected
when the record answers, so the page does not jump. Ask Qellys answers the same question ("how did last night's
reports do"). Ask also learned the day's parlay changes: the record of the tickets built since the 19 November
rebuild, said apart and including the ones still waiting on their games; that the Record counts one set a game; what
a ticket's card says under it (a leg that is not the report's own pick is named); and why a game has fewer than two
parlays or none yet, in the report's own words (props still to be bought, too few of the report's picks priced, none
that fit). One bug found on the way: Ask named a league's three-leg parlays "three" and its two-leg ones "two" when
reading the real record (its test fed it the wrong key). Checked by
tests/test_the_last_slate_s_reports_are_summed_at_a_glance.py and tests/test_ask_reads_the_reports_and_the_races.py.

**ZD. The heartbeat says what became of each report pick, and the Record's one set a game is said everywhere** (step
792; 19 November). Nothing to run. Two things. First, a count: each game's parlays are its report's own picks, and
on Thursday three Sunday games' reports carried 12 player picks of which the board priced 3 as legs. Steps ZB and
ZC's notes said what the other nine were (tackles, a benched market, scorers) from the code, not from a count. The
heartbeat now counts it for each league, over its games still to play (pick_fates): how many of the reports' player
picks are legs at 60% or better (strong), legs the fill may take at 50 to 60% (fill), priced but under 50% once
corrected (low), in a market no parlay carries (no_parlay: tackles, sacks, kicking), in a benched market (benched),
priced as a leg only at another number (other_line), a matchup pick no leg source holds (matchup_only), a scorer
only the touchdown field prices (scorer_only), a row a leg source holds and will not use (refused), or on none of
the board's lists (absent). Counts only: no pick's name rides in it. If the counts show picks that should be legs
and are not (other_line, matchup_only), that is the next fix. Second, a re-check of today's work found the one-set-
a-game rule (step YI) said in one place and contradicted in three. Under a finished game on How our reports did, the
line about earlier versions still ended "Every one counts on the Record"; it now says the Record counts the set the
report carried at the start, and a game from before 16 November (every version listed) says the Record counts none
of them. Ask Qellys says the same when asked about a finished game's parlays. And one lost ticket no longer reads "1
of the 1 ticket that lost missed by a single leg": it reads "The one ticket that lost missed by a single leg." An
idea measured and not built the same evening: marking a market's legs down from its Most Likely record (college
passing yards said 65% and hit 53% over 79 picks). The Most Likely board already has a per-market correction that
must pass a held-out test before it is saved (engine/likelycal), and one market in sixty running two standard errors
cold is what chance alone produces, so a second, weaker correction on top would have been learning from noise. A
replay of the current builder on every finished game since 16 November (the report's picks with the book's price
standing in for our chance, which the free view does not carry) says what the rebuilt tickets would have done: NBA
17 of 52 three-leg tickets (33%) against the 1 of 15 posted under the old rules, hockey 16 of 36 (44%) against 5 of
18, two-leg tickets 25 of 45 and 18 of 29. Small samples, and partly the games the unders rule was changed on; the
real record from 19 November's games on is what counts, and the Record page shows it apart. Checked by
tests/test_the_heartbeat_says_what_became_of_each_report_pick.py,
tests/test_every_finished_game_marks_its_picks_and_parlays.py, tests/test_each_league_records_its_game_parlays.py
and tests/test_ask_reads_the_reports_and_the_races.py.

**ZC. A game short of picks a parlay can use takes our Most Likely picks for it**
(step 791; 19 November). Nothing to run. With step ZB live the NFL's three-leg tickets went from 5 to 11 (two-leg 0
to 2), and four Sunday games had their two. Five Sunday games still had none: their reports carry 15 player picks,

Likely picks of ours the report's card had no room for (it lists four, one a player), and the Most Likely board's
numbers hit what they claim (the NFL's 62.2% said, 61.7% hit, over 2,036 picks; the NBA's and hockey's run above
what they say). So a game still short of its two after the usual fill may now take its Most Likely picks in the
report's picks' places: only at 60% or better, only on a ticket that clears 25% by our numbers, the report's own
picks still first, and each such leg named on the ticket ("a Most Likely pick for this game the report's card did
not list"). Any other prop still rides one a ticket beside two of the report's, as step YU set. A game that stays
short says so, and that its Most Likely picks made no ticket either. The heartbeat counts the tickets they stood in
on (threes_board_filled). Checked by tests/test_the_parlays_are_built_to_win.py and
tests/test_the_parlays_are_made_of_the_reports_picks.py.

**ZB. The legs' pull toward the books learns from today's legs, not the retired ones**
(step 790; 19 November). Nothing to run. Step ZA's counts answered it within the hour: the eight Sunday games short
of the report's picks carry 24 player picks, 11 the parlays may use (the rest are tackles, quarterback completions,
benched for losing money, and the like), and 5 of those 11 stand at 50% or better once corrected. The correction was
the NFL's learned pull toward the books: 1.0, every leg dragged all the way to the book's number. It was learned
from every leg ever graded, mostly the retired source (any priced prop, before 16 November's credibility rule),
which hit 13 points under what we said; the picks the legs are now, the Most Likely board's, hit what they claim
(62.2% said, 61.7% hit, 2,036 NFL picks). The shift beside it already learned only from legs built the current way,
so the retired source could not hold the honest legs to its errors; the pull now does too. A league with fewer than
sixty graded legs built the current way keeps our own numbers until it has them (the NFL's 1.0 is out the moment
this is live: a share written under the old rule is no share until the next settle pass refits it), and the
heartbeat's leg_fit says so. Checked by tests/test_parlay_legs_learn_their_league_s_correction.py.

**ZA. The heartbeat says why a game is short of the report's own picks**
(step 789; 19 November). Nothing to run. With step YY live, the NFL's ten Sunday games short of their two three-leg
tickets said why: eight are "few_picks", fewer than two of the report's own picks among the game's priced legs at
50% or better, two have picks that do not fit together. The likeliest reason is the legs' learned correction
(engine/legfit): it pulls each league's legs, and each market's, toward what they have hit, and the NFL's receptions
legs hit 42% on the record where we said 71%, so a receptions pick the report likes at 62% can stand under 50% as a
leg, and no ticket is built on a leg we expect to lose. The heartbeat now says, for the games short of picks, how
many picks their reports carry, how many the board prices at any chance and how many stay at 50% or better once
corrected, and the correction itself (the share toward the book, the shift, each market's shift: the model's
numbers, no pick). The morning check-in reads them and, if the correction is holding the NFL's Sunday legs back on
old evidence, fixes it. Checked by tests/test_every_game_report_posts_its_three_leg_parlays.py.

**YZ. A report's own picks are never crowded out of its parlays by the game's other props**
(step 788; 19 November). Nothing to run. Found while reading why the Sunday games were short. A game short of its
two three-leg tickets fills from a pool of fourteen legs: the report's picks at 60% or better, then the rest. Every
ticket takes two of the report's own picks, but the rest were sorted by our chance alone, so a game's other props at
60% and better took the fourteen places ahead of the report's picks at 50-60%, and the fill had none of them to
build with. A hockey game prices about a hundred props, and the NFL's Sunday games about forty once bought, so the
more a game was priced, the likelier its own picks were pushed out. The report's picks now enter the pool first,
then the best of the rest. Checked by tests/test_the_parlays_are_built_to_win.py (on the old order the case builds
nothing: none of the report's three picks reached the pool).

**YY. A Sunday game whose props are bought says why it is short, not that its props are still to come**
(step 787; 19 November). Nothing to run. Sunday's props were bought this afternoon, as step YW meant: the NFL board
now carries 453 player props priced across the 12 games through Sunday, where at 4:17 PM it had 51, all Thursday's;
a passing-yards line for nearly every quarterback, receptions and receiving yards for about half the players; 30
touchdown pairs (3 before) and 82 Most Likely picks (36). The month's balance went from 48,063 to 47,656 credits
across that hour's pulls. But the three-leg tickets stayed at five, and ten Sunday games still read "bought from
three days before it ... once the books post them": a game inside its buying days that was short of its two kept the
calendar's word whatever was on file (step YQ's stray prop or two). From ten priced props a game's are bought now,
and short of its two it says the real reason, as every other game does, and that the books post more of its props as
it nears. The heartbeat counts that reason, with a new one, few_picks: fewer than two of the report's own picks
among its priced legs (a ticket takes two). The far pull's second run of the day and Friday's two buy what the books
post next. Checked by tests/test_every_game_report_posts_its_three_leg_parlays.py.

**YX. Two unders from one game share a ticket: the report's strongest picks reach its parlays**
(step 786; 19 November). Nothing to run. The parlay rules killed any ticket with two unders from one game, as a
"script clash" (two legs that need the game to go opposite ways). Two unders need the same game, a quiet one, and
the doctrine's clash list never names them. So a report whose best picks were unders could make no three-leg ticket
at all: Bruins at Red Wings on 18 November had seven under picks (five hit) and no parlay, and so did Avalanche at
Utah the same night, and Kings at Bruins, Stars at Golden Knights and Ducks at Blues the night before. The finished
games' own picks say the pair was never a clash: two different players' unders in one game hit together 52% of the
time, against 53% if they were unrelated (163 pairs), the same as two overs (44% against 45%, 447 pairs), and an
under picked by the report hit 72-76% where an over hit 64-71%. So two unders now share a ticket, priced like two
overs. Two teammates under on the same stat stay apart, as their overs always have (one pie: one player's big night
is the other's quiet one), except hockey's points, where one goal is a point for up to three skaters. An over that
needs scoring still never shares a ticket with an under that needs a quiet game. Replayed on the hockey and NBA
reports of 16-18 November, today's builder now makes three-leg tickets for 36 of the 41 games (27 before), and 33 of
their 87 tickets hit (38%) where 22 of 64 did before (34%). Tonight's hockey, NBA and college football games short
of their two tickets for a conflict (seven of them at 4:25 PM) are read again on the next build. Checked by
tests/test_the_parlays_are_built_to_win.py and tests/test_college_parlays_build_and_stay_tracked.py.

**YW. Sunday's NFL props from Thursday, so the weekend's reports have their parlays days ahead**
(step 785; 19 November). Nothing to run. Your answer to decision 9 ("Yes ... buying Sunday's props 2 to 3 days
early. Yes to all that") is in: the NFL's board now buys the books' player props for the games up to three days
after tonight's, so Sunday's games get their picks and parlays from Thursday, Monday night's from Friday and the
next Thursday's from Monday. College football keeps the day before. So tonight's pulls do not buy Sunday's dozen
games every time they re-price the Thursday game, the far games ride two of the NFL's pulls a day at most, six hours
apart, counted only once a pull lands, at their own slice of the day's credits (a quarter at most) on top of what
tonight's game already had; every other pull stays tonight's and tomorrow's. One far pull of Sunday's slate costs
about 364 credits (thirteen or fourteen games at 26), so a normal week adds about 1,600 credits: two pulls on
Thursday and two on Friday, and a game or two more on Saturday's, Monday's and Tuesday's. A game report waiting on
its props now says when they come: "bought from three days before it, on Friday", or inside those three days, that
its parlays are built once the books post them (the books post some Sunday props late in the week). The first far
pull goes as soon as this is live, so Sunday's reports should have their parlays tonight. Checked by
tests/test_credits_go_to_tonights_games.py and tests/test_every_game_report_posts_its_three_leg_parlays.py.

(step 784; 19 November). Nothing to run. Your three games now have a name, a deeper report and a record of their

(Eastern, from 6 PM, so Thanksgiving's day games are not Thursday nights; the Lions' Thanksgiving game is a Lions

have more of the report's own picks to be built from (tonight's Colts at Texans had no three-leg ticket because its
four picks clashed). Its card on the NFL page wears a Featured ribbon (where Top game sits), and its report says at
the top what it is, "Featured · Thursday night", with how the reports on games like it have done so far. And the
featured games keep a record apart, on Report Picks and on the Record page's NFL tab under How our reports did:
every featured game, Lions games, Thursday nights and Monday nights, each with the report's picks won and lost and
the units at one unit a pick, the parlays its report carried at kickoff, and who we said would win; then each game;
and a Featured games chip that lists only those games with every pick and parlay checked or crossed. It starts with
three games from week 10: the Commanders at Giants on 12 November (nothing of its report was on the record yet), the
Patriots at Lions (its tickets from before the record kept a starting set, so none count) and the Chargers at Ravens
on Monday night (picks 2-6, its three-leg parlay and touchdown pair both lost). Ask Qellys answers from the same
record ("how have the Monday night reports done?"). College football's Thursday games are not in it; say if you want

**YU. A ticket is two of the report's picks at least, and a short game may add one other prop**
(step 783; 19 November). Nothing to run. With step YR live, the boards rebuilt under the new rules: the NBA's four

record supports: every ticket carries at least two of the report's own picks, and a game short of its two may add

tests/test_the_parlays_are_built_to_win.py and tests/test_the_parlays_are_made_of_the_reports_picks.py.

tests/test_the_parlays_are_built_to_win.py.

**YS. The Record page says how the rebuilt parlays do, apart**
(step 781; 19 November). Nothing to run. So you can see whether step YR's parlays win without the older tickets
mixed in, each league's parlay card on the Record page now says how the tickets built since the rebuild have done,
under its totals: "Since 19 Nov's rebuild (stronger legs, honest chances): 7 of 12 hit, where we gave them 31% ·
+9.6u · 4 waiting on their games". It counts each game's starting set from 19 November's games on (the rules went

tests/test_the_parlays_are_built_to_win.py.

**YR. The parlays are built to win: honest chances, the report's own picks, no losing markets**
(step 780; 19 November). Nothing to run. You asked for parlays that win and make money. What the record says (every
graded ticket, read 19 November): the 1,321 tickets we priced with a link between their legs ("one passing game
feeds both") hit 382, where the link said 443 and the legs on their own said 407, so the link made our chance too
high and pushed us toward the wrong tickets. Since the parlays were built from each report's own picks (17
November), hockey's three-leg tickets hit 4 of 10 against about 33% said and the NBA's two-leg ones 9 of 11 against
45%; before that, a prop the report never picked hit 62% as a leg against 75% for its picks. And the record pays a
won ticket at the card's own "take it at" price, so a ticket makes money there exactly when it hits more often than
we said. Four changes: (1) a ticket's chance no longer counts a link between its legs unless the record shows linked
legs hit together; that weight is fitted every night from the graded tickets and starts at zero, so the chances on
the cards are the legs' own and the tickets chosen are the ones with the strongest legs; (2) a game short of two
three-leg parlays fills with the report's own picks first (down to 50%, as they hit above what we say), and takes a
prop the report did not pick only at 60% or better, where step YN let them in at 50%; (3) a market benched for
losing money (the NFL's completions, the NBA's points) is no parlay leg; (4) the bars a ticket clears are said
without the link: 40% for two picks, 25% for three (two and three picks at 63%). Checked by
tests/test_the_parlays_are_built_to_win.py; the morning check-in reads how they do.

(step 779; 19 November). Nothing to run. With step YO live at 12:56 the NFL board had an entry for all 13 games, and

**YP. A game short of two three-leg parlays can fill from any three props at 50% that fit**

**YN. Games still short of two three-leg parlays fill with legs down to 50%**
(step 776; 19 November). Nothing to run. The first builds after YH went live left games short: the heartbeat read

with the error's type). Tomorrow's check-in reads it. Checked by
tests/test_every_game_report_posts_its_three_leg_parlays.py.

**YM. The first visit trimmed, not its budget raised: 5.4 KB of room again**
(step 775; 19 November). Nothing to run. You, asked whether to raise the first visit's size budget or trim it, with

(step 774; 19 November). Nothing to run; the roster step that runs every half hour does it. You, asked whether
college players should show their real positions: "I would assume so. Yeah." College basketball's roster page and

players without one position among them. The roster step now reads each Division I school's published roster from

page says how many are waiting. The player search and the player pages read positions from that file, so they show
them too. The file drops its empty fields, as college football's does. A player no current roster lists (Cameron
Boozer, in the NBA now) shows no position in the search rather than the box score's starter mark. Live by 16:54 UTC:
216 schools read on the first run, 3,301 players with a position, Cayden Boozer a guard. Checked by
tests/test_college_players_show_their_real_positions.py.

**WS. A game's parlays lead with its two strongest picks, and every ticket clears a bar of its own** (step 729; 18
November). Nothing to run. Ethan, over How our reports did (picks 6 of 11 and parlays 0 of 4; picks 4 of 5 and
parlays 0 of 3; picks 7 of 8 and parlays 2 of 9): "how are we winning so many picks ... but losing so many parlays?
... Make it so the parlays win as well", and of the NFL's three-leg tickets on paper: "track them and learn and make
them better". The record was right; the tickets were the problem. Three picks must all hit, and at the 68% the NBA's
report picks hit, three together come in about three times in ten: that night three of a game's picks hit together
one time in five (96 of 480), two of them two times in five (86 of 220) and the two shortest-priced 5 of 8, and 85
of the NBA's 151 lost three-leg tickets lost by a single leg. So each game now leads with its two strongest picks as
a two-leg ticket, and its next two as a second (no pick on both), each only at 42% or better by our numbers; a
three-leg ticket is made only at 30% or better (one we give less than that we expect to lose seven times in ten),
and a game whose picks make fewer says why. The two-leg tickets are journaled apart (game_two), graded, counted on
the Record page, on Report Picks and on the finished game's card, and go on paper on their own record (40 graded
under 36%), so the easier ticket never brings the harder one back. And the legs now learn market by market: the
league's correction was one number for all its markets, and they do not miss alike (the NFL's receptions legs hit
42% where we said 71%, hockey's shots on goal 79% where we said 66%), so each market with 40 graded legs learns a
shift of its own, kept only when it scores the newest legs better. The NFL's and the NBA's three-leg tickets stay on
paper until they hit 25% again; both sizes are graded either way.

Nothing to run. You asked that the site always carries the most up-to-date information, so every public feed on the

again every 30 seconds while a game is live, every two minutes otherwise, and whenever you come back to it. The NFL

night of games is a handful of builds. The daily rebuild of every league is unchanged. Second, a standings page

for the WNBA). The page still waits on the next season in an offseason, as you asked in August; whether it should

lists the colour fade's two files among the trimmed copies it serves, which rides along with 00k whenever you run
it; until then the full copies are served and nothing is missing.

**WM. A team's page wears its club's colours, and every colour change fades** (step 723; 17 November). Nothing to
run. Your two answers: team pages should wear their club's colours, and the switch between your own colours and a
team's should be smooth, not a quick glitchy switch. A team's page now puts the whole screen on that club's two
colours while it is open, the way a player's page does: over your own colours if you wear some, and with the setting
off too; at night the crest and name lie on the colours themselves. Leaving the page gives the screen back to your
colours, or the site's gold, and one club's page goes straight to the next's. The pair is the club's real colours
(the Leafs' blue with a deeper blue, not the fog grey their white trim turns into), the same pair a player's page
uses. And every change of the screen's colours now cross-fades over about four tenths of a second: your colours to a
club's and back, one player's page to the next, into and out of a game's page, the theme. It is done by laying a
copy of the old look over the new one and fading the copy out, so the phone does it without repainting anything, and
nothing fades for someone who asked their phone for less motion. The button on a team's page now reads "Wear these
everywhere": the page wears them already, so the button says what it adds. The fade's code loads after the first
paint, so the first visit is no heavier.

**WL. A game that ends after its board has moved on is still fact-checked** (step 722; 17 November). Nothing to run.
Building the welcome page's numbers showed How our reports did holding 14 NFL games, 12 of college basketball, 8 of

have been checked (in any league: a box score that lands after the board has moved had the same end). Now the report
kept before the start, with its picks and parlays, is graded against the history's own final and archived once its
box score is in, for a day after the game leaves the board, and the build's line says "N more archived after leaving
the board". Reproduced both ways on a college final: on the board (the ordinary path grades it) and off it (the new
one does). Tuesday's three college games are the first to finish since the fact checks began; the overnight check
reads them.

**WI. A parlay that took a team to win is graded on the game** (step 719; 17 November). Nothing to run; RUN_NEXT 00n

or whose own row never graded, grades from the same prop settled in our other pick lists, on its own line from the
player's real number; and one no list holds gets its own row written on the ticket's day, which the box score then
grades like any other pick (a player who sat voids). Measured on the live record the minute it went out: the NFL's
22 tickets still waiting all graded, and Magic at Celtics went from nine to one; six of those read void on Derrick
White's assists and Jalen Suggs's rebounds, both of whom played, and the re-audit reopens and grades them off the

**WH. A game's parlays are made of its report's own picks** (step 718; 17 November). Nothing to run; RUN_NEXT
00n is an optional check. Your two screenshots of How our reports did (Monday's NBA: picks 4 of 5 and parlays 0 of
3, picks 6 of 7 and parlays 1 of 6) asked how the picks could hit and the parlays not, when the parlays use those

Heat shows it plainly: the four picks on its tickets all hit, and every ticket lost on a leg the report never
picked (Bam Adebayo over 0.5 threes, twice). Built from the picks alone, Monday's tickets would have hit 7 of 25
where they hit 4 of 30 (NHL: 1 of 5 where 1 of 8). Now each game's three-leg tickets are built inside its report,
once its picks are known, from those picks and nothing else, under every rule a leg kept: the 60% floor, no

fewer than four tickets posts fewer and says why, and the card's parlay line and the short version name the same
tickets. The touchdown pairs are the touchdown research's own and did not change.

The dashes: a ticket "waiting on the box score" days after its game (nine of Magic at Celtics', and six to nineteen
on every NFL game of the 15th). A ticket's legs are journaled on paper first, and that journal refuses a game
already under way, so a board built just before a start and journaled just after it wrote the tickets and not
their legs: those legs never had a row to grade from. Such a leg now voids once the rest of its ticket has graded
(the game is over), the way a book voids a leg it cannot settle, and no new ticket is journaled without its legs'
rows. The waiting ones clear on the nightly settle by themselves. A player who never played was not the cause:
outside football the no-show sweep already voids those once the night's games are final.

**WG. The tab bar stays on the screen's foot as you scroll** (step 717; 17 November). Nothing to run.
Your two screenshots from the Duo, the bar halfway up over the picks (beside DraftKings and on its own), had one

the keyboard's place). The pinned layers then hold to the foot of that short screen while the page scrolls down,
and come back as it scrolls up: the bar moving as you scroll. The nudge from step RK (the game chat bar, 15 November) could not clear it, because
iOS still believes in the keyboard. Now the app reads how far the screen stands from the place the layers are
pinned to, every frame the page moves, and moves every pinned layer back by exactly that much: the bar, the live
pill, the game chat's button, the toasts, the gold light, the top bar, the strip under the clock, and the sheets
and dialogs. It lets go the moment iOS puts things back, or a field of the app's own takes the keyboard (the bar
steps aside for that as before), or you pinch to zoom. Only the installed app does this (the Home Screen app and
the iOS build); a Safari tab and Android phones are untouched, and when nothing is wrong nothing moves at all. The
nudge no longer moves the page when the screen is still short by a keyboard, where it could only jog the page under
your thumb. If the bar ever stands up the screen again, a screenshot of it on the same page is all I need.

On the game page, until kickoff, whatever landed after the report was written shows as a card over the report,

**VI. Any time: take the All-Star and exhibition games out of the NBA's and the WNBA's history** (step 693; 17
November). Two commands, seconds each. Checking the live player pages, Caitlin Clark's 2026 game log held 47 games
and a club called "SPO": ESPN files the WNBA's All-Star Game (25 July, "SPO" against "COOP", 129-122) and an
exhibition against Nigeria's national team (2 May, 105-57) as games of the season, so the nightly kept their box
scores, and every number read off a player's games counted them: the page's averages and league places, the
boards' recent form and hit rates, the Game Log, and the Nigeria game as a win in Indiana's record. It is not one
game: the live logs show every WNBA All-Star Game since 2023 (Team USA against Team WNBA in 2024) and exhibitions
against Puerto Rico and Japan's Toyota Antelopes, and the NBA's too: 2025's All-Star tournament (Chuck's, Kenny's
and Shaq's teams, the Rising Stars) and 2026's World, Stars and Stripes, mini-games of a few minutes that sit in the
NBA's season-to-season rates. The nightly now stores a game only when both sides are the league's own clubs, and
says what it leaves out. The first command
lists what was stored before (each game's day, sides and how many players' lines) and writes nothing; paste it
back. The second removes them:

```
cd /srv/qellys && sudo -u qellys python3 -m engine.hoopsexhibitions
```

```
cd /srv/qellys && sudo -u qellys python3 -m engine.hoopsexhibitions --apply
```

If the list holds a real club (one that joined a league and is not yet in engine/divisions), don't run the second;
tell me which, and it goes into the table first.

**VH. Optional, any time: fill the WNBA pages' shooting numbers** (step 692; 17 November). One command, a few
minutes. The basketball box scores have kept shots (field goals, threes and free throws made and tried) since 20
October, and the WNBA's 2026 season ended before that, so its pages have no FG%, 3P% or FT% (step VF puts minutes
in the headline instead). This re-reads every 2026 WNBA game day from ESPN's free summaries, about 300 requests,
and writes the missing columns beside the ones already there; nothing is removed. Paste back the last line
(`N days re-read, N player lines written`). The pages pick the numbers up within six hours, or at the next restart:

```
cd /srv/qellys && sudo -u qellys nice -n 19 python3 -c "from engine import db; from engine.sources import espnhoops as h; c = db.connect(); days = [r[0] for r in c.execute(\"SELECT DISTINCT period FROM games WHERE sport='wnba' AND season=2026 ORDER BY period\")]; n = sum(h.ingest_day(c, d, league='wnba').get('player_logs', 0) for d in days); c.commit(); print(len(days), 'days re-read,', n, 'player lines written')"
```

**UB. The playoff race is drawn as a bracket** (step 660; 17 November). Nothing to run. Your ask, over the NFL's
seed lists: "the playoff page should be layed out as a bracket and not this chart". The NFL's "If the season ended
today" and college football's "If it started today" are now brackets. The NFL's: each conference as the playoffs run,
the 1 seed beside its bye and then 4 v 5, 3 v 6 and 2 v 7 in the Wild Card column, each club with its logo, seed, record
and why it is in ("6-0 · North leader", "5-1 · Wild card"); then the divisional round, the conference title game and the
Super Bowl, with thin lines joining every game to the one its winner plays next. The rounds after the first say who
meets whom in words ("Lowest seed left", "Wild Card winner"), never a guessed winner, and a note says the divisional
round is reseeded. On a computer the AFC runs left to right, the Super Bowl sits in the middle and the NFC is mirrored on
the right, the way a printed bracket looks; on a phone the AFC, the NFC and the Super Bowl stack, each swiping sideways
through its rounds with the next round peeking in, so no name is squeezed. Under it the clubs just outside are listed
per conference with how far back of the 7 seed they are ("Just outside in the AFC: Bengals 5-5, 1 game back of the 7
seed; Colts 5-5, level"). College football's twelve draw the same way: the four first-round games on the better seed's
campus, each feeding the bye seed it meets (8/9 to the 1, 5/12 to the 4, 7/10 to the 2, 6/11 to the 3), the
quarterfinals, the semifinals (the 1 and 4 sides, the 2 and 3 sides) and the title game, with the first four out under
it. The bracket shows to everyone; the chances below it stay a member's.

and pairs but no single picks. What has settled shows to everyone, as every settled bet on the Record does; one still waiting

page gets the same marks.

0% keeps our number, 100% takes the book's. The share it uses is the one that would have scored its graded legs best,
and only when it also scores the newest 30% better (they are held out of the fit); until a league has 60 graded legs,
or when the newest do not get better, its legs stay as they are. The 3-leg tickets' legs and the touchdown or scorer
pairs' learn apart. A leg is corrected before it is held to the 60% floor, so a leg that only cleared it on an
overstated number is no longer a leg. Legs journaled before today kept no book's chance, so their own price stands in.
The fit runs after each settle pass that grades a ticket, beside the one-club bar; the settle log says
"parlays: nfl:three legs now pulled N% toward the books' chances (…)" when a league's share moves, and each board's
game parlays carry the share in force (`counts.leg_fit`). The journal now keeps our own chance beside the posted one
(`p_raw`), so the correction is always learned on our number and never on top of itself.

**TR. A parlay leg's chance is one our own pick rules stand behind** (step 650; 16 November). Nothing to run. You
asked why football's stated chances run 10 to 30 points too high. They did on the game parlays' legs, and only there:
- the record that morning: the NFL's legs hit 49.9% against the 68.4% we gave them (catches 34% against 71%), college's
  56.2% against 71.2% (passing yards 31% against 76%). The scorer pairs' legs hit what we said (NFL 44.9% against
  42.2%), and the NFL's Most Likely picks in the same 60-75% band did too (65.9% against 65.7%, 1,259 picks); college's
  ran 4 points high (61.9% against 65.6%), not the 15 its legs did;
- the cause: since 14 November (step QS) a game's parlays could take any prop the board prices, at the chance the Edge
  picks show. That chance is pulled halfway to the book's, so a main line near even money shows 60% only when our raw
  number sits 16 points or more above the book's, past the 10 points where the Edge picks refuse a number as a data
  error. The board kept those props for its other lists and the parlays took them. Our number beat the line on only 47%
  of the NFL's catch props and 42% of college's passing-yard props, so a gap that wide was noise. And when two lists
  priced the same bet, the parlay kept the higher chance;
- now, in every league (the builder is shared; football is where it showed): a priced prop joins a parlay only when the
  Edge picks would stand behind its number (no refusal, within 10 points of the book's chance). The same bet's Most
  Likely chance speaks for it first, then an Edge pick's, then any other priced prop's. Each leg keeps where it came
  from and the book's chance;
- the Record page's leg line counts each bet once (a leg on three tickets counted three times) and gives the books'
  chance beside ours;
- each leg is graded on its own line. The journal keeps one row for a player's market and side, at the first line
  written (a football week shares one date), and a leg at another line took that row's result: an over 3.5 could grade
  won off an over 1.5's row. A leg at another line is now graded on its own line from the player's real number, and
  every settle pass re-grades the tickets already graded the old way. The newest 144 graded legs had no such case, so
  this did not make the gap, but it could have.

The next boards built are the first built this way. The legs already graded stay on the record, changed only where a
leg had taken another line's result. If football's new legs still run high once about 100 are graded, a correction learned from each league's record, the way
the basketball and hockey boards learned theirs (step PP), is the next step, and yours to say yes to.

**TO. The player search answers in well under a second, once you stop typing** (step 647; 16 November).
Nothing to run. Checking your "players are not showing up" message, I timed the live league search: college
football took 8 to 16 seconds a search ("arch manning" 15.6 s), the NBA up to 5.9 s, the NFL 1 to 4 s. Every letter
typed paid two costs. The logs were searched with a pattern no index can serve, so each letter read every row the
league has (millions for college). And every rostered player (41,888 in college football) went through the spelling
matcher to pad the list. On top of that the page sent one search per letter, so the box worked through a dozen slow
searches before it reached the name you typed. Now:
- each league's names are kept in memory: built at start (one index lookup per name, about 5 MB for college

- the page asks the league once you pause typing (0.28 s) and shows "Searching NFL players" while it waits.
At college football's scale on my machine: a real name in 2 to 5 ms, a misspelling in about 0.3 s (it was 1.1 s here
and about 15 s on the box). If a rebuild ever fails, the service log says "the <league> name list was not rebuilt",
and the search keeps the list it has.

The stored copies are still there, though, and grading and the board read them. Please run these two (neither


The second says whether the college team map knows Ohio State's and Texas's ESPN numbers (a copy keyed

From those I'll know whether `--apply` clears them again or a writer needs fixing first.

**TL. A full page for every player, with ESPN's menus** (step 644; 16 November). Nothing to run. You sent
ESPN's page for Josh Allen and asked for every player in every sport to have a page that looks like it, with
each menu. Open any player (search a name, or tap a player anywhere on the site) and the Players page now
becomes that player's page, in every league we keep box scores for: NFL, college football, NBA, WNBA, college
basketball, NHL and MLB.
- **The header:** the club's colours with its logo large and faint behind, the headshot, the name, then
  "Buffalo Bills · #17 · QB" and "6'5" · 237 lb · Age 30", with any injury tag under them.
- **Six menus under it:** Overview, News, Stats, Bio, Splits and Game Log.
  - **Overview:** the season's four numbers, each with where it ranks in the league this season (a
    quarterback's YDS, TD, INT and passer rating; a runner's CAR, YDS, TD and yards a carry; a receiver's REC,
    YDS, TD and yards a catch; a basketball player's points, rebounds and assists a game and FG%; a skater's G,
    A, PTS and SOG; a goalie's SV%, GAA, saves and starts; a hitter's H, HR, TB and PA; a pitcher's K, IP, K/9
    and games). Then the previous game (both clubs, the score, both records through that game, and four of
    the player's numbers from it), a splits table (that game, its month, that opponent, home or away, and the
    season), the last five games and the latest news, then tonight's markets (the card this page always showed).
  - **News:** the roster's latest injury note and any move between clubs, then the headlines that name the
    player or the club, each linking to its source.
  - **Stats:** season by season and the career line (totals; basketball shows a game's average, as its box
    score is read).
  - **Bio:** team, position, number, height, weight, birthday and age, birthplace, college, years in the
    league, shooting hand (hockey), status, and the seasons and games we have on file.
  - **Splits:** the season a game's average at a time: all of it, the last five, home and away, wins and
    losses, each month and each opponent, with a season picker.
  - **Game Log:** the full game log from step TK, inside the page.
- **How the ranks work:** a total ranks among everyone with one; a basketball average among players with at
  least half the games of a regular (the 90th percentile of games played, so one name several college players
  share, whose games the file adds up together, can't raise the bar for everyone); a rate (passer rating, FG%, yards a carry, save
  percentage) and a count where fewer is better (interceptions, goals against) among players with at least
  40% of the leader's volume. Ties share a place, and "fewest" marks the fewer-is-better ones. The server
  builds every league's rank tables in the background a minute after it starts and rebuilds them every six
  hours, so no page waits on them (built cold, MLB's took 5.7 seconds and college basketball's 7.5).
- **What isn't there, and why:** ESPN's QBR isn't in our files, so the quarterback strip uses the passer
  rating. Draft details, longest plays and sacks aren't in our box scores. College and baseball rosters list
  no height, weight or age, so those headers show what the rosters do have. News is headlines and links only,
  like the rest of the site's news; when no headline names the player, the club's show, and the league's when
  nothing names either. Baseball's previous game shows no club records: MLB's games table is filled as slates
  are read, so a record counted from it would be wrong (it gave the Dodgers 29-19-1 in October).
- **Players with no game on file yet** (a freshman or a backup the roster lists) get the page too: the header
  and Bio from the roster, News, and a line saying no games are on file yet, where the numbers go.
- **A game whose box score isn't in yet** (a player's row filed the night of the game, before the week's box
  scores land) now says "Box score not in yet" in the game log and "The box score isn't in yet" on the page,
  and isn't counted in games played, totals or averages until its line arrives. The game log shipped earlier
  today counted it as a game of zeros: on the live file Joe Burrow's Sunday game did exactly that, which put
  his average at 2,386 yards over 9 games (265 a game) instead of over 8 (298).
It reads the box scores and rosters the site already keeps, is free like the game log, and the server keeps
each player's page five minutes.

The passer rating is the NFL's own formula (college uses its passer efficiency): Burrow's 25 of 35, 254 yards,
